first_step_test: One lopsided head oval joined to one smaller muzzle oval gives the learner a readable face base while leaving the ears, expression, body, and prop areas open.

source.notes: The approved fourth six-panel landscape sheet uses foreground-first banana construction and square cells. Two earlier sheets were rejected for a closed torso line hidden by the banana, and a third was rejected because its square canvas produced rectangular cells; all remain private under rejected-progressions.

final_elements.name: two ears and three-point hair tuft
final_elements.description: Exactly two round ears attached at different heights and one three-point tuft centered above the forehead.

final_elements.name: asymmetrical face

frames.visible_job: Draws one lopsided round head and one attached low muzzle oval.
frames.instruction: Draw one lopsided round head, then overlap its lower half with one smaller wide muzzle oval. Keep the top, both sides, and all paper below the head open for the ears, hair, body, and banana.

frames.visible_job: Adds two ears, one three-point tuft, and the complete asymmetrical face.
frames.instruction: Attach exactly two round ears at slightly different heights and add one three-point tuft above the forehead. Draw one wide oval eye looking sideways, one narrow crescent eye, one raised eyebrow, two nostril dots, and one off-center open grin with exactly two square teeth.
adds: two ears and three-point hair tuft
introduces: two ears and three-point hair tuft

frames.visible_job: Adds one curved banana below the head, then two attached arms and hands around it.
frames.instruction: Below the muzzle, draw one upward-curving banana with a short stem at each end. Attach exactly two arms from beneath the head and close exactly two simple hands around the banana ends, stopping every arm line at the prop edge.
adds: banana with two arms and hands
introduces: banana with two arms and hands

frames.step_name: Wrap the torso behind the snack
frames.visible_job: Adds one seated torso around the foreground banana and one long spiral tail.
frames.instruction: From beneath the head, curve the torso sides down around the outside of both arms and join them with a low rear body curve behind the banana. From the lower rear body, sweep one long tail outward and curl its tip into one open spiral.
adds: torso behind banana and curled tail
introduces: torso behind banana and curled tail

frames.step_name: Seat the legs and add finish marks
frames.visible_job: Adds two bent legs, one belly patch, three banana seams, and one teal broken shadow.
frames.instruction: Attach exactly two bent seated legs beneath the torso with one simple foot each, letting them overlap the lower body edge. Curve one belly patch behind the banana, add exactly three short peel seams along the fruit, and fill one broad broken ground shadow beneath the feet with teal marker.
adds: two seated legs and belly patch
three banana seams and teal broken shadow
introduces: two seated legs and belly patch
three banana seams and teal broken shadow

final_step.visible_job: Fills established monkey, muzzle, banana, belly, ear, hand, and foot shapes with directional marker strokes and small paper gaps.
final_step.instruction: Fill the established monkey warm brown, the muzzle, ear centers, belly patch, hands, and feet peach, and the one banana golden yellow with orange along its lower edge. Keep the same teal shadow and eye highlight, leave a few small paper gaps in the brown tuft and fur, and strengthen existing black contours without adding shapes.
adds: marker color and small highlight gaps in established regions

visual_review.first_step_observation: The first saved crop contains only one bold lopsided head oval and one attached wide muzzle oval at their final anchors. The empty top, side, and lower paper clearly reserves the later hair, ears, expression, banana, limbs, and body without front-loading the drawing.
visual_review.draw_through_observation: I compared all six saved square crops pairwise at full size. The head, expression, foreground banana, hands, arms, torso, tail, legs, belly patch, peel seams, and ground shadow keep their anchors; the foreground-first order avoids hidden chest lines, and the final adds color and small paper gaps without new structure.

landmark_observations.head and muzzle: The lopsided head and low wide muzzle keep the same outline, overlap, and page position.
landmark_observations.two ears and three-point hair tuft: One round ear attaches higher at left, one lower at right, and a clearly countable three-point tuft interrupts the established top contour.
landmark_observations.asymmetrical face: The left eye is a wide oval with a sideways dark pupil and white glint, the right eye is a narrow squint, one eyebrow arches above the wide eye, two nostrils sit on the muzzle, and the off-center open grin contains two square teeth.

transitions.observed_addition: Two ears, the three-point tuft, and a deliberately mismatched face turn the simple head base into a distinct monkey character.
transitions.instruction_match: The copy matches the ear height difference, tuft count, eye shapes and gaze, single raised brow, two nostrils, and two-tooth grin visible in the crop.
